messages:
Hannah: CI flagged a weird typing edge in sample-app where generated client methods expose very loose return types after we started preserving unknown enum strings. mypy complains in one place but pyright is fine.
Lin: what's the concrete failure?
Hannah: gist of mypy output:
```
src/clients/orders_client.py:120: error: Item "str" of "Union[OrderStatus, str]" has no attribute "name"  [attr-defined]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 20 source files)
```
Hannah: the code assumes `order.status.name` when it's an Enum, but we now allow raw str so mypy flags it. Runtime previously worked because it was always Enum.
Omar: two paths: 1) make generated models preserve Enum as primary type and add a separate `raw_status` field for unknowns (keeps callers clean), or 2) keep union type and generate thin `.pyi` stubs that refine types for common access patterns (e.g., typed property `status_enum` that returns Optional[OrderStatus]`).
Lin: I like stubs for minimal disruption. Many consumer projects ignore type-check errors when library internals are fuzzy; providing a .pyi for enhanced DX is non-breaking.
Vik: Stubs would help pyright and mypy without forcing annotation changes. We can emit a simple property in stubs like:
```
@property
def status_enum(self) -> Optional[OrderStatus]: ...
```
then docs can show callers use `.status_enum` when they need enum-specific methods.
Hannah: good idea. Also suggest generator adds an inline comment in the runtime model pointing to the typed helper in the stubs so users discover it.
Omar: minor impl notes: 1) update packaging to include generated .pyi files; 2) ensure stubgen output is deterministic across runs; 3) add a typing CI job that runs both mypy and pyright against the stubs.
CI-bot: sample-app/mypy-check failed on 1991234567-branch  https://ci.internal/runs/7801  logs attached.
Lin: who wants to prototype? I can add a small generator patch that emits a `*.pyi` alongside the model with the `status_enum` convenience property and keep runtime file as `Optional[Union[OrderStatus, str]]` plus the fallback validator.
Hannah: also add a tiny code example to docs showing safe access: `if order.status_enum is not None: do_enum_things(order.status_enum)` else fallback to raw string handling. That'll reduce confusion.
Omar: add unit tests to sample-app: one test exercising `status_enum` property types (reveal_type), one runtime test with unknown value, and packaging test ensures .pyi included.
Vik: open PR with generator change + packaging update + sample-app tests + docs snippet. Mention pyright/mypy parity in PR description.
CI-bot: PR 4555 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autogen/pull/4555 
CI-bot: PR 4555 CI: mypy+pyright checks passed, unit tests passed and merged at 1991234630.
Hannah: thanks everyone. after merge I'll run a smoke-check across quickstart and playground to confirm nothing else breaks.
Lin: resolving thread on my end. :white_check_mark:
